<p id="mwDQ">The <b id="mwDg">Isdal Woman</b> (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_language" title="Norwegian language" about="#mwt14" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwDw" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"langx","href":"./Template:Langx"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"no"},"2":{"wt":"Isdalskvinnen"}},"i":0}}]}">Norwegian</a><span about="#mwt14">: </span><i lang="no" about="#mwt14">Isdalskvinnen</i><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_containing_Norwegian-language_text" about="#mwt14" id="mwEA">, <abbr title="circa" about="#mwt15" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwEQ" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"circa","href":"./Template:Circa"},"params":{},"i":0}}]}">c.</abbr> 1930–1945 – November 1970) is a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Placeholder_name" title="Placeholder name" id="mwEg">placeholder name</a> given to an unidentified woman who was found dead at Isdalen ("The Ice Valley") in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bergen" title="Bergen" id="mwEw">Bergen</a>, Norway, on 29 November 1970.</p>

<p id="mwFA">Although police at the time ruled a verdict of likely <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide" title="Suicide" id="mwFQ">suicide</a>, the nature of the case encouraged speculation and ongoing investigation in the years since.<sup about="#mwt18" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-BT_2-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"BT"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-BT-2"}}"><a href="#cite_note-BT-2" id="mwFg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwFw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGA">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Half a century later, it remains one of the most profound <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_case" title="Cold case" id="mwGg">cold case</a> mysteries in Norwegian history.<sup about="#mwt19" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-BT_2-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"BT"}}"><a href="#cite_note-BT-2" id="mwGw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwHA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwHQ">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwHg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt20" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_3-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3" id="mwHw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwIA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIQ">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwIw" data-mw="{"autoGenerated":true}"></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwJA" aria-labelledby="Discovery"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Discovery">Discovery</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isdal_Woman&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Discovery"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwJQ"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SvartediketUlrikenIsdalen23Juni1.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwJg"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SvartediketUlrikenIsdalen23Juni1.jpg" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/SvartediketUlrikenIsdalen23Juni1.jpg/250px-SvartediketUlrikenIsdalen23Juni1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/SvartediketUlrikenIsdalen23Juni1.jpg/500px-SvartediketUlrikenIsdalen23Juni1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="2000" data-file-height="1330" data-file-type="bitmap" height="166" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwJw"></a><figcaption id="mwKA">Isdalen, where the woman was discovered.</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwKQ">On the morning of 29 November 1970, a man and his two young daughters were hiking in the foothills of the north face of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulriken" title="Ulriken" id="mwKg">Ulriken</a>, in an area known as Isdalen ("Ice Valley"); it was also nicknamed "Dødsdalen" ("Death Valley") due to the area's history of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide" title="Suicide" id="mwKw">suicides</a> in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages" title="Middle Ages" id="mwLA">Middle Ages</a> and more recent hiking accidents.<sup about="#mwt21" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_3-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3" id="mwLQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwLg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwLw">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwMA">]</span></span></a></sup> They came across the charred body of a woman located among some <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scree" title="Scree" id="mwMQ">scree</a>.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="2" id="mwMg" aria-labelledby="Investigation"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Investigation">Investigation</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isdal_Woman&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Investigation"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwMw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bergen_Police,_Norway" title="Bergen Police, Norway" class="mw-redirect" id="mwNA">Bergen police</a> responded quickly and launched a full-scale investigation, filed as case name "134/70". Examining the site, police noted the woman's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supine_position" title="Supine position" id="mwNQ">supine position</a>, her clenched hands up by her torso and the evidence of a nearby campfire. The front of her body and her clothes had been severely burned, and her face was unrecognisable. Also located or placed near the body, and affected by the fire, were an empty bottle of St. Hallvard <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liqueur" title="Liqueur" id="mwNg">liqueur</a>; two plastic water bottles; a plastic passport holder; rubber boots, a woolen jumper and a scarf; nylon stockings; an umbrella,<sup about="#mwt24" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-4"}}"><a href="#cite_note-4" id="mwNw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwOA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwOQ">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwOg">]</span></span></a></sup> purse, and a matchbox. There was also a watch, two earrings and a ring. Around the body were traces of burned paper, and beneath it was a fur hat which was later found to have traces of petrol.<sup about="#mwt27" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-5"}}"><a href="#cite_note-5" id="mwOw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwPA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwPQ">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwPg">]</span></span></a></sup> All identifying marks and labels on these items had been removed or rubbed off.</p>

<p id="mwPw">Three days later, investigators found two suitcases belonging to the woman which had been abandoned at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bergen_Station" title="Bergen Station" class="mw-redirect" id="mwQA">Bergen railway station</a>.<sup about="#mwt31" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Isdalen_Mystery_2016_6-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Isdalen Mystery 2016"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Isdalen_Mystery_2016-6"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Isdalen_Mystery_2016-6" id="mwQQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwQg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQw">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwRA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt32" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_3-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3" id="mwRQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwRg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwRw">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwSA">]</span></span></a></sup> In the lining of one suitcase, police discovered five <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Mark#Banknotes" title="Deutsche Mark" id="mwSQ">100 Deutsche Mark notes</a> (<abbr title="circa" about="#mwt28" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwSg" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"c.","href":"./Template:C."},"params":{},"i":0}}]}">c.</abbr> US$137 in 1970).<sup about="#mwt35" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-7"}}"><a href="#cite_note-7" id="mwSw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwTA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwTQ">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwTg">]</span></span></a></sup> Among other items, they also found clothing, shoes, wigs, makeup, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eczema" title="Eczema" class="mw-redirect" id="mwTw">eczema</a> cream, 135 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_krone" title="Norwegian krone" id="mwUA">Norwegian kroner</a>, Belgian, British and Swiss coins, maps, timetables, a pair of non-prescription glasses, sunglasses with partial fingerprints that matched to the woman,<sup about="#mwt36" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Isdalen_Mystery_2016_6-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Isdalen Mystery 2016"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Isdalen_Mystery_2016-6" id="mwUQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwUg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUw">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwVA">]</span></span></a></sup> cosmetics and a notepad.<sup about="#mwt37" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_3-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3" id="mwVQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwVg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwVw">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwWA">]</span></span></a></sup> All identification information had been removed from the items.<sup about="#mwt38" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_3-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3" id="mwWQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwWg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwWw">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwXA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwXQ">An <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autopsy" title="Autopsy" id="mwXg">autopsy</a> at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haukeland_University_Hospital" title="Haukeland University Hospital" id="mwXw">Gades Institutt</a> concluded the woman had died from a combination of incapacitation by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenobarbital" title="Phenobarbital" id="mwYA">phenobarbital</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_monoxide_poisoning" title="Carbon monoxide poisoning" id="mwYQ">poisoning by carbon monoxide</a>.<sup about="#mwt39" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Isdalen_Mystery_2016_6-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Isdalen Mystery 2016"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Isdalen_Mystery_2016-6" id="mwYg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwYw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZA">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZQ">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soot" title="Soot" id="mwZg">Soot</a> was found in her lungs, indicating she was alive as she burned, and her neck was bruised, possibly from a fall or blow. Analysis of the woman's blood and stomach showed that she had consumed between 50 and 70 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenemal" title="Fenemal" class="mw-redirect" id="mwZw">Fenemal</a> brand sleeping pills,<sup about="#mwt42" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-8" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-8"}}"><a href="#cite_note-8" id="mwaA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwaQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwag">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwaw">]</span></span></a></sup> and found next to her body were a further twelve sleeping pills. At autopsy, her teeth and jaw were removed due to her unique dental work, and tissue samples of her organs were taken.<sup about="#mwt43" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_3-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3" id="mwbA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwbQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbg">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwcA">Police then launched an appeal for information in the Norwegian media regarding the case. The last time she was seen alive had been on 23 November, when she checked out of Room 407 of the Hotel Hordaheimen. Hotel staff told police that she was good-looking and roughly <span about="#mwt44" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwcQ" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"convert","href":"./Template:Convert"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"1.63"},"2":{"wt":"m"},"abbr":{"wt":"on"}},"i":0}}]}">1.63</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt44"> </span><span about="#mwt44">m (5</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt44"> </span><span about="#mwt44">ft 4</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt44"> </span><span about="#mwt44">in)</span> tall, with dark brown hair and small brown eyes. Staff noted that the woman kept mainly to her room and seemed to be on guard. When she checked out, she paid her bill in cash and requested a taxi. Her movements between then and the discovery of her body remain unknown.</p>

<p id="mwcg">Police were able to decode the notepad entries, and determined that they indicated dates and places the woman had visited.<sup about="#mwt47" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-9" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-9"}}"><a href="#cite_note-9" id="mwcw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwdA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwdQ">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwdg">]</span></span></a></sup> As a result, based on handwritten check-in forms, police determined that the woman had travelled around Norway (i.e., <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo" title="Oslo" id="mwdw">Oslo</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trondheim" title="Trondheim" id="mweA">Trondheim</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stavanger" title="Stavanger" id="mweQ">Stavanger</a>) and Europe (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris" title="Paris" id="mweg">Paris</a>) with at least eight fake <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passport" title="Passport" id="mwew">passports</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudonym" title="Pseudonym" id="mwfA">aliases</a>.<sup about="#mwt50" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-10" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-10"}}"><a href="#cite_note-10" id="mwfQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwfg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwfw">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwgA">]</span></span></a></sup> While details such as birthdays and occupations changed from one form to another, she consistently gave her nationality as Belgian; the forms were filled out in either German or French.<sup about="#mwt51" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_3-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3" id="mwgQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwgg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwgw">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwhA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt52" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Isdalen_Mystery_2016_6-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Isdalen Mystery 2016"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Isdalen_Mystery_2016-6" id="mwhQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwhg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwhw">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwiA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwiQ">These were her false identities:</p>

<ul id="mwig"><li id="mwiw">Geneviève Lancier, place of birth <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leuven" title="Leuven" id="mwjA">Leuven</a>, living at Rue Sainte-Walburge 2, Leuven</li>
<li id="mwjQ">Claudia Tielt, place of birth <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels" title="Brussels" id="mwjg">Brussels</a>, living at Place Saint-Walburge 17, Brussels</li>
<li id="mwjw">Claudia Tielt, place of birth Brussels, living at Rue de la Madeleine 3, Brussels</li>
<li id="mwkA">Claudia Nielsen, place of birth <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghent" title="Ghent" id="mwkQ">Ghent</a>, living at Rue Sainte-Walburge 18, Brussels</li>
<li id="mwkg">Alexia Zarne-Merchez, place of birth <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ljubljana" title="Ljubljana" id="mwkw">Ljubljana</a>, living at Rue St. Hildegaarde 81, Brussels</li>
<li id="mwlA">Vera Jarle, place of birth <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp" title="Antwerp" id="mwlQ">Antwerp</a> (the form with address in Brussels has been lost)</li>
<li id="mwlg">Fenella Lorck (the form with an address in Brussels has been lost)</li>
<li id="mwlw">Elisabeth Leenhouwer, birthplace <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostend" title="Ostend" id="mwmA">Ostend</a>, living at Philipstockstraat 44A, Brussels.</li></ul>

<p id="mwmQ">With the exception of Rue de la Madeleine, all street names also turned out to be false.</p>

<p id="mwmg">It was also learned that the woman previously stayed at several hotels in Bergen, and was known to change rooms after checking in.<sup about="#mwt55" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-11" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-11"}}"><a href="#cite_note-11" id="mwmw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwnA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwnQ">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwng">]</span></span></a></sup> She often told hotel staff that she was a travelling saleswoman and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiquities" title="Antiquities" id="mwnw">antiquities</a> dealer. One witness said that she overheard the woman talking to a man in German in a Bergen hotel. Others who met her mentioned that she also spoke <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_dialects" title="Flemish dialects" id="mwoA">Flemish</a> or broken English and smelled of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garlic" title="Garlic" id="mwoQ">garlic</a>.<sup about="#mwt56" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Isdalen_Mystery_2016_6-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Isdalen Mystery 2016"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Isdalen_Mystery_2016-6" id="mwog"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwow"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpA">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt59" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-12" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-12"}}"><a href="#cite_note-12" id="mwpg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwpw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwqA">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwqQ">]</span></span></a></sup> People who saw or met her also commented that she wore <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wig" title="Wig" id="mwqg">wigs</a>.</p>

<p id="mwqw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composite_sketch" title="Composite sketch" class="mw-redirect" id="mwrA">Composite sketches</a> of the unknown woman, based on witness descriptions and analysis of her body, were circulated in many countries via <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpol" title="Interpol" id="mwrQ">Interpol</a>. Despite the significant police resources deployed, the woman was never identified and the case was quickly closed.<sup about="#mwt60" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_3-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3" id="mwrg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwrw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwsA">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwsQ">]</span></span></a></sup> While authorities concluded that she had committed suicide by ingestion of sleeping pills,<sup about="#mwt61" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-BT_2-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"BT"}}"><a href="#cite_note-BT-2" id="mwsg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwsw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwtA">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwtQ">]</span></span></a></sup> others believe that there is evidence that she was murdered.<sup about="#mwt64" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-13" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-13"}}"><a href="#cite_note-13" id="mwtg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwtw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwuA">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwuQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="3" id="mwug" aria-labelledby="Burial"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Burial">Burial</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isdal_Woman&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Burial"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwuw"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Møllendal_kirkegård.JPG" class="mw-file-description" id="mwvA"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Møllendal_kirkegård.JPG" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/M%C3%B8llendal_kirkeg%C3%A5rd.JPG/250px-M%C3%B8llendal_kirkeg%C3%A5rd.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/M%C3%B8llendal_kirkeg%C3%A5rd.JPG/500px-M%C3%B8llendal_kirkeg%C3%A5rd.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="3264" data-file-height="2448" data-file-type="bitmap" height="188" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwvQ"></a><figcaption id="mwvg">Møllendal cemetery, where "The Isdal Woman" is buried.</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwvw">On 5 February 1971, the woman was given a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholicism" title="Catholicism" class="mw-redirect" id="mwwA">Catholic</a> burial (based on her use of saints' names on check-in forms) in an unmarked grave within the Møllendal graveyard located in Bergen. Attended by sixteen members of the Bergen police force, she was buried in a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zinc" title="Zinc" id="mwwQ">zinc</a> coffin to preserve her remains and for ease of disinterment. Her ceremony was also photographed in case relatives came forward at a later date.<sup about="#mwt65" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_3-8" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3" id="mwwg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwww"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwxA">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwxQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="4" id="mwxg" aria-labelledby="Theories"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Theories">Theories</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isdal_Woman&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Theories"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwxw"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Agm119_penguin.png" class="mw-file-description" id="mwyA"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Agm119_penguin.png" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/Agm119_penguin.png/250px-Agm119_penguin.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/56/Agm119_penguin.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled 2x" data-file-width="252" data-file-height="177" data-file-type="bitmap" height="176" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwyQ"></a><figcaption id="mwyg">Norwegian Penguin missile.</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwyw">Much remains unanswered about the case, especially the reasons for the woman's many identities and unexplained travel plans, which raise the question of espionage or criminal activity.<sup about="#mwt66" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Isdalen_Mystery_2016_6-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Isdalen Mystery 2016"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Isdalen_Mystery_2016-6" id="mwzA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwzQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwzg">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwzw">]</span></span></a></sup> Multiple investigations point to the possibility that she was a spy,<sup about="#mwt69" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_3-9" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-:0-3"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3" id="mw0A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw0Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw0g">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw0w">]</span></span></a></sup> given the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War" title="Cold War" id="mw1A">Cold War</a> context of the period. Norway had experienced other strange disappearances in the 1960s, close to military installations, which traced back to international espionage.<sup about="#mwt72" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-14" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-14"}}"><a href="#cite_note-14" id="mw1Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw1g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw1w">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw2A">]</span></span></a></sup> The declassified records of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Armed_Forces" title="Norwegian Armed Forces" id="mw2Q">Norwegian Armed Forces</a> also reveal that many of the woman's movements seem to correspond to top secret trials of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_(missile)" title="Penguin (missile)" id="mw2g">Penguin missile</a>.<sup about="#mwt75" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-15" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-15"}}"><a href="#cite_note-15" id="mw2w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw3A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw3Q">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw3g">]</span></span></a></sup> A fisherman is also reported to have seen the woman in the area of Penguin missile testing in Stavanger;<sup about="#mwt78" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-16" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-16"}}"><a href="#cite_note-16" id="mw3w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw4A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw4Q">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw4g">]</span></span></a></sup> her presence in Stavanger is corroborated by a shoe salesman who sold her a pair of rubber boots.<sup about="#mwt79" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Isdalen_Mystery_2016_6-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Isdalen Mystery 2016"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Isdalen_Mystery_2016-6" id="mw4w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw5A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw5Q">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw5g">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="5" id="mw5w" aria-labelledby="Later_developments"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Later_developments">Later developments</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isdal_Woman&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Later developments"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mw6A">The taxi driver who took the woman from the hotel to Bergen railway station was never found. In 1991, however, a taxi driver wishing to remain anonymous said that after picking up the unknown woman at the hotel, they were joined by another man for the ride to the railway station.<sup about="#mwt82" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-17" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-17"}}"><a href="#cite_note-17" id="mw6Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw6g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw6w">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw7A">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mw7Q">In 2005, a Bergen resident, who was aged 26 in 1970, told a local newspaper that after seeing the sketch circulated, he had suspected that the Isdal Woman was a woman he had seen five days before the body was discovered, when he was hiking on the hillside at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fløyen" title="Fløyen" id="mw7g">Fløyen</a>. Surprisingly, she was dressed lightly for the city rather than a hike, and was walking ahead of two men wearing coats who looked "southern".<sup about="#mwt85" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-18" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-18"}}"><a href="#cite_note-18" id="mw7w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw8A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw8Q">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw8g">]</span></span></a></sup> The woman appeared resigned and seemed about to say something to him but did not. He went to someone he knew at the police to report this incident, but was told to forget about it.<sup about="#mwt88" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Yndestad_19-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Yndestad"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Yndestad-19"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Yndestad-19" id="mw8w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw9A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw9Q">[</span>19<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw9g">]</span></span></a></sup> Therefore, neither the man's name nor his alleged sighting was recorded at that time.</p>

<p id="mw9w">After the case was reopened in 2016,<sup about="#mwt89" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Isdalen_Mystery_2016_6-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Isdalen Mystery 2016"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Isdalen_Mystery_2016-6" id="mw-A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw-Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw-g">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw-w">]</span></span></a></sup> Norwegian broadcaster <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRK" title="NRK" id="mw_A">NRK</a> commissioned the American artist <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Missal" title="Stephen Missal" id="mw_Q">Stephen Missal</a> to create six alternative sketches of the Isdal Woman, which were shown to people who had seen her.<sup about="#mwt92" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-New_Sketches_20-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"New Sketches"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-New_Sketches-20"}}"><a href="#cite_note-New_Sketches-20" id="mw_g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw_w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQA">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAQI">In 2017, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isotope_analysis" title="Isotope analysis" id="mwAQM">stable isotope analysis</a> of the woman's teeth (taken from her unburied jawbone<sup about="#mwt93" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:1_21-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":1"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:1-21" id="mwAQQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAQU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQY">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQc">]</span></span></a></sup>) indicated that the woman had been born in about 1930, plus or minus four years, in or near <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuremberg" title="Nuremberg" id="mwAQg">Nuremberg</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weimar_Republic" title="Weimar Republic" id="mwAQk">Germany</a>, but had moved to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Third_Republic" title="French Third Republic" id="mwAQo">France</a> or the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France–Germany_border" title="France–Germany border" id="mwAQs">France–Germany border</a> as a child.<sup about="#mwt96" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-22" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-22"}}"><a href="#cite_note-22" id="mwAQw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAQ0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQ4">[</span>22<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQ8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt99" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-23" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-23"}}"><a href="#cite_note-23" id="mwARA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwARE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARI">[</span>23<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARM">]</span></span></a></sup> This reinforced earlier analysis of the woman's handwriting, which suggested that she had been educated in France or a neighbouring country.<sup about="#mwt100" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Isdalen_Mystery_2016_6-8" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Isdalen Mystery 2016"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Isdalen_Mystery_2016-6" id="mwARQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwARU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARY">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARc">]</span></span></a></sup> Analysis also indicated she had been to a dentist in either East Asia, Central Europe, Southern Europe or South America.<sup about="#mwt103" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-NRK_Dokumentar_2016_24-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"NRK Dokumentar 2016"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-NRK_Dokumentar_2016-24"}}"><a href="#cite_note-NRK_Dokumentar_2016-24" id="mwARg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwARk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARo">[</span>24<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARs">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt106" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-25" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-25"}}"><a href="#cite_note-25" id="mwARw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAR0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAR4">[</span>25<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAR8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwASA">In 2018, NRK and the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_World_Service" title="BBC World Service" id="mwASE">BBC World Service</a> published a podcast series titled <i id="mwASI"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_in_Ice_Valley" title="Death in Ice Valley" id="mwASM">Death in Ice Valley</a></i>, which included interviews with eyewitnesses and forensic scientists, also suggesting that the Isdal Woman's birthplace may have been southern Germany or the French-German border region, and that she was probably born in or around 1930.<sup about="#mwt109" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-26" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-26"}}"><a href="#cite_note-26" id="mwASQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwASU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASY">[</span>26<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASc">]</span></span></a></sup> She was also probably raised in French-speaking Belgium.<sup about="#mwt112" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-27" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-27"}}"><a href="#cite_note-27" id="mwASg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwASk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASo">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASs">]</span></span></a></sup> In June 2019, the BBC revealed that listeners of the podcast had given more clues.<sup about="#mwt115" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:1_21-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":1"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-:1-21"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:1-21" id="mwASw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAS0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAS4">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAS8">]</span></span></a></sup> Further, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colleen_M._Fitzpatrick" title="Colleen M. Fitzpatrick" id="mwATA">Colleen Fitzpatrick</a>, a geneticist with the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_Doe_Project" title="DNA Doe Project" id="mwATE">DNA Doe Project</a>, contacted the <i id="mwATI">Death in Ice Valley</i> team to offer her help in identifying the woman through <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genealogical_DNA_test" title="Genealogical DNA test" id="mwATM">genetic genealogical isotope testing</a> of autopsied tissues.<sup about="#mwt116" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:1_21-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":1"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:1-21" id="mwATQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwATU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATY">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATc">]</span></span></a></sup> It has since been revealed that she is of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_mitochondrial_DNA_haplogroup" title="Human mitochondrial DNA haplogroup" id="mwATg">mtDNA haplogroup</a> H24, indicating a matrilineal line of descent originating in South East Europe or South West Asia. The woman also seems to have had a French passport based on the fact that an unidentified French national was registered on one of the flights she took to Norway.<sup about="#mwt119" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-28" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-28"}}"><a href="#cite_note-28" id="mwATk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwATo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATs">[</span>28<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAT0">Author Dennis Zacher Aske proposed that the Isdal Woman was a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_work" title="Sex work" id="mwAT4">sex worker</a>, based on the way that her route was planned (goal-oriented and always returning to the same point, probably her home), her wish to remain anonymous, her behaviour at hotels (including marking the doors in different ways) and the fact that the different men she was witnessed meeting never came forward. Aske argued that another person was probably at the crime scene when the woman died, based on evidence from the scene and her medically intoxicated condition in the hours before her death. He noted there were arguments that supported the death being either murder or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assisted_suicide" title="Assisted suicide" id="mwAT8">assisted suicide</a>, believing murder to be most likely.<sup about="#mwt122" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-29" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-29"}}"><a href="#cite_note-29" id="mwAUA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAUE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUI">[</span>29<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAUQ">In 2019, after a publication of an article in the French newspaper <i id="mwAUU"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Républicain_Lorrain" title="Le Républicain Lorrain" id="mwAUY">Le Républicain Lorrain</a></i>,<sup about="#mwt125" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-30" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-30"}}"><a href="#cite_note-30" id="mwAUc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAUg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUk">[</span>30<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUo">]</span></span></a></sup> a resident of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbach" title="Forbach" id="mwAUs">Forbach</a> claimed to have had a relationship with the Isdal Woman in the summer of 1970. According to this informant, the woman was a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multilingualism" title="Multilingualism" id="mwAUw">polyglot</a> with a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balkan" title="Balkan" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAU0">Balkan</a> accent who often dressed herself up to look younger than her age (between 36 and 44), refused to share personal details and often received scheduled phone calls from abroad. Looking through the woman's belongings, the informant found various wigs, colorful clothes and a photograph of the woman riding a horse. Suspecting she was a spy, he considered contacting the authorities but was afraid to do so. Both the informant's story and the photograph were published in a subsequent issue of the newspaper.<sup about="#mwt128" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-31" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-31"}}"><a href="#cite_note-31" id="mwAU4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAU8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVA">[</span>31<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAVI">On June 12, 2023, an article in <i id="mwAVM"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neue_Zürcher_Zeitung" title="Neue Zürcher Zeitung" id="mwAVQ">Neue Zürcher Zeitung</a></i> suggested that the Isdal Woman may have had connections with the Swiss banker <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/François_Genoud" title="François Genoud" id="mwAVU">François Genoud</a>, and that <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Intelligence_Service" title="Norwegian Intelligence Service" id="mwAVY">Norwegian Intelligence Service</a> (<i id="mwAVc">E-tjenesten</i>) interfered with local police investigations. The newspaper sourced the suggestion to a "professional fact-checker".<sup about="#mwt129" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-32" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-32"}}"><a href="#cite_note-32" id="mwAVg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAVk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVo">[</span>32<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
